project_outcome.statement: No improved zero-density coefficient, prime-interval endpoint, or L-function-family transfer is proved. The checked baseline remains density coefficient 30/13, with uniform and almost-all interval endpoints 17/30 and 2/15.

why_active_gate_matters.statement: Cycle 63 isolates the actual positive-exponential weighted pair census whose strict X^(17/25) improvement would advance E13. Cycles 165--176 conditionally compile a critical fixed-beta census into terminal webs and exact transport/divisor classifiers, but none proves the census or actual branch population. The upstream analytic census, not another terminal classifier, is now the active bottleneck.

progress_criterion.statement: By the Cycle-216 gate, the pivot must prove P<=X^(17/25-epsilon) for some fixed epsilon>0, prove an equivalent strict actual-curve census margin that survives reinsertion, or rigorously realize an actual positive-exponential saturator supporting a materially larger saturation theorem. Cycles 177--216 test determinant/large-sieve and bilinear-spacing mechanisms plus adversarial saturators. A new finite transport/interface classifier without actual population is non-progress; if no viable mechanism or saturator survives, promote E11/E12 and target a complete-form saving strictly greater than 3/50. Cycle 500 is the hard terminal project cap.

cold_start_handoff.deferred_work: Cycles 165--176 are parked as a conditional inverse toolkit until actual population enters an existing terminal branch. E14D-L, boundary denominators, direct interval propagation, and L-function transfer are deferred. Paper-stage hostile audit begins only after a manuscript theorem is frozen.
